name: Box
description: The lowest-level layout primitive: a polymorphic box with spacing props, leaving surfaces and colors to className.

anatomy.description: The rendered tag; div by default, swapped through the as prop.
Padding and margin shorthands that follow the spacing scale; axis values override the all-sides value.
Colors, radius and shadows arrive through className tokens, not Box props.

dos: Use the as prop to give the wrapper a meaningful landmark or grouping element.
Reach for Box for one-off spacing wrappers instead of writing a bespoke utility class.
Apply surface and color tokens through className utilities.
donts: Don't arrange multiple children with Box; Flex or Stack expresses that intent.
Don't combine Box margins with a parent's gap; the spacing doubles up.
Don't use Box where a named component like Card or Section already exists.

examples.title: Spacing and surface
examples.description: Numeric padding follows the spacing scale while surface tokens arrive through className.

examples.title: Semantic element
examples.description: The as prop swaps the rendered tag, here a centered section with per-axis spacing.

guidance.useWhen: You need a one-off wrapper with spacing and surface styling and want to avoid writing a bespoke class.
guidance.avoidWhen: You are arranging multiple children along an axis; Flex or Stack expresses that intent better.
guidance.behavior: Box renders no styling of its own beyond the spacing props; axis values (px, py, mx, my) override the all-sides value.
guidance.responsive: Spacing props are static; combine Box with responsive Tailwind classes for breakpoint-dependent layouts.

notes: Box renders a div by default; use the as prop to give the content a meaningful landmark or grouping element.
Box adds no visual styling or behavior beyond its spacing props; focus order and semantics come entirely from its children.
